sampling_model.design: Observational or randomized binary treatment with conditional exchangeability and i.i.d. superpopulation sampling.
sampling_model.units: Each unit supplies baseline \(X\), treatment \(Z\), at-risk history, first readmission history, terminal-event history, and administrative censoring through \(\tau\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every supported covariate cell has positive mass and both treatment arms have positive probability.
sampling_model.censoring: Within each realized arm \(z\), \(C\) is conditionally independent of that arm's pair \((D(z),R(z))\) given \(X\), and \(G_{zx}(u)\ge\gamma\) through \(\tau\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Marked product-limit or IPCW estimation of \(\mu_{zx}\), \(G_{zx}\), and \(p_x\); the multiplier expansion remains the open inference node.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Defines two-index TV-SACE and RM-SACE and estimates them by posterior imputation under parametric illness--death shared-frailty models without imposing \(D(0)\leq D(1)\); that fitted family is generally incomparable with the present monotonicity-restricted nonparametric class.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Theorem 1 and the three-horizon nonidentification corollary

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Uses finite-IV contrasts to identify unequal survivor-complier outcome submeasures and solves a fixed-stratum scalar benefit partial-transport problem by exact-mass threshold cuts.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Theorem 1, which instead proves the Borel marked deadline fiber and jointly sharp changing-cohort TV/RM surface image

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Lifts endpoint partial couplings to full finite-IV compliance and selection laws that reproduce the observed distribution.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Theorem 1, which instead lifts every feasible marked coupling to a four-event-time semicompeting-risk law

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.1 gives sharp fixed-time SACE bounds by integrating pointwise symbolic linear-program bounds.
Theorem 7 characterizes existence of a probability measure with prescribed marginals under support inequalities.
Characterizes sharp bounds for continuous functionals of latent joint potential-outcome laws through random-set inequalities and linear programs.
Represents generic known-marginal causal partial-identification problems by multi-marginal optimal transport and proves rates for selected quadratic costs.
Derives partial-identification bounds for semi-competing-risk effects under a single population stratification.
Bootstraps randomly perturbed finite linear-program values to obtain uniformly valid inference for linear-moment identified sets.
Proves conditional weak convergence of an increment-level wild bootstrap for multivariate Nelson--Aalen processes under censoring.
Establishes derivative-based valid resampling for directionally differentiable maps when the ordinary bootstrap fails.
Develops uniform resampling for optimized value functions using estimated directional derivatives.
Sharpens scalar SACE bounds with detailed survival histories and ranked-average-score restrictions while indexing cross-world survival dependence by a copula parameter.
Represents sharp bounds on functionals of the joint potential-outcome distribution as optimal-transport values and estimates them through the dual.
Derives central-limit and Hoeffding-type results for inverse-probability-of-censoring-weighted estimators under right censoring.

body.tldr: Death truncates readmission, so the two-index TV-SACE and RM-SACE surfaces depend on an unidentified cross-world assignment of treated readmission times to control death times. After the proved full-horizon IPCW recovery lemma identifies the complete within-arm laws, and under the additional maintained order \(D(0)\le D(1)\), the note characterizes the complete sharp monotonicity-restricted surface by a necessary-and-sufficient marked-capacity lift, proves common fixed-cohort extremizers and exact RM integration, and gives a certified three-horizon law whose joint cross-cohort support is strictly narrower than its coordinate rectangle. Quadratic chain flows, qualitative continuous-grid convergence, and deterministic-grid finite-sample outer containment make the population characterization computable. A joint marked-product-limit/IPCW functional limit, root-\(n\) grid-bias control, and simultaneous multiplier bands remain open.

project_justification.gap: Comment et al. define clinically meaningful TV-SACE and RM-SACE surfaces but leave their cross-world law to a parametric illness--death shared-frailty model and do not impose terminal monotonicity.  The closest accepted-bank comparison, \texttt{pid\_slate\_benefit\_partialtransport\_v1/thm:sharp-exact-mass-threshold-interval} together with \texttt{pid\_slate\_benefit\_partialtransport\_v1/thm:full-law-endpoint-attainment}, identifies unequal survivor-complier outcome submeasures from finite-IV contrasts, solves a fixed-stratum scalar benefit partial transport, and lifts endpoint couplings to full IV-selection laws.  It does not establish the Borel readmission-marked deadline fiber, four-event-time semicompeting-risk lift, or jointly sharp changing-cohort TV/RM surface image proved here.
project_justification.niche: After separately auditing the additional restriction \(D(0)\le D(1)\), each always-survivor cohort becomes a nested marked-resource selection problem.  The contribution is the marked continuous-time fiber and its simultaneous changing-cohort surface image, not capacity projection or full-law lifting in generic terms.  This monotonicity-restricted nonparametric class is a subclass of the unrestricted causal model but is generally incomparable with Comment et al.'s fitted shared-frailty family.
project_justification.fill: The note proves the monotonicity-restricted if-and-only-if marked-capacity image, a measurable four-event-time full-law lift, common fixed-cohort extremizers on \(S(t)\geq\eta\), exact RM integration, an atomic strict cross-cohort support certificate, quadratic computation with a dual infimum, qualitative continuous approximation under the bounded finite-part coordinate-density envelope alone, and deterministic-grid finite-sample outer containment with \(D=\tau\) retained in the last bin. The continuous approximation needs no Lipschitz-density restriction. The separated-bump extension and smooth nonidentification transfer hold on every explicit envelope regime \(M\geq M_\delta\), \(L_{\mathrm{Lip}}\geq L_\delta\); no claim is made for arbitrary smaller fixed envelopes or for enlarged-class capacity sharpness.

body.related_work: Comment, Mealli, Haneuse, and Zigler (2025) define the TV-SACE and RM-SACE estimands and estimate them with a Bayesian illness--death shared-frailty model.  The present equality is instead a sharp nonparametric characterization after adding the audited restriction \(D(0)\le D(1)\); it is not an equality result for their unrestricted nonmonotone causal class, and their fitted shared-frailty family is generally incomparable with this class.  The closest in-repository result is the accepted \texttt{pid\_slate\_benefit\_partialtransport\_v1}: its \texttt{thm:sharp-exact-mass-threshold-interval} uses finite-IV contrasts to identify unequal survivor-complier outcome submeasures and solves a fixed-stratum scalar benefit partial transport, while \texttt{thm:full-law-endpoint-attainment} lifts endpoint couplings to full IV-selection laws.  The present theorem does not claim novelty for capacity projection or full-law lifting generically; it adds the Borel marked \( (D(0),R(1)) \) fiber under every deadline/mark capacity, a measurable lift to four semicompeting-risk event times, and the jointly sharp changing-cohort TV/RM surface image.  Yang and Ding (2018) use detailed survival histories and copula sensitivity for scalar SACE bounds.  Nevo and Gorfine (2022) study semi-competing-risk bounds under one population stratification.  Chen, Cui, and Yang (2024) integrate scalar fixed-time bounds but do not prove common readmission-threshold extremizers.  Strassen (1965) supplies the closed-relation coupling criterion; the marked cut reduction and its four-time adaptation are proved here.  Russell (2021), Ober-Reynolds (2023), and Gao, Ge, and Qian (2024) provide generic latent-law and transport programs, whereas the quadratic nested chain is specific to the terminal order.  Goldberg (2019) supplies IPCW concentration tools.  Cho and Russell (2024), Bluhmki et al. (2019), Fang and Santos (2019), and Firpo, Galvao, and Parker (2023) inform the still-open simultaneous-inference route.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The finite-sample outer set contains the truth on a deterministic grid, including allowed death mass at \(D=\tau\), but a quantitative shrinking rate under simultaneous grid refinement is not yet proved.  At tied deadline cuts the sharp endpoint map is only directionally differentiable, so ordinary centered multiplier validity is not asserted.  The smooth strict-support witness applies only when the declared density and Lipschitz envelopes dominate the explicit fixed-kernel constants.  Full-horizon censoring support remains essential because an endpoint for an early survivor cohort can depend on treated death information later than that cohort horizon.
body.honest_scope: The marked-capacity image is sharp only over nonparametric full laws satisfying the maintained terminal-monotonicity restriction \(D(0)\le D(1)\), in addition to the stated exchangeability, event-order, overlap, and full-horizon censoring conditions.  It is not asserted to equal the identified set in Comment et al.'s unrestricted nonmonotone class.  Standardized fixed-cohort bounds and RM integration are asserted only where \(S(t)\geq\eta>0\).  When \(0<\eta\leq1/4\), the atomic lifts transfer nonidentification to every larger class containing them.  For a fixed separated kernel, the smoothed pair belongs to, and transfers nonidentification within, every envelope class satisfying \(M\geq M_\delta\) and \(L_{\mathrm{Lip}}\geq L_\delta\); no smooth-witness claim is made for arbitrary smaller fixed envelopes.  Neither witness transfers capacity sharpness.  The joint marked-process functional central limit theorem, estimated-censoring expansion, root-\(n\)-negligible grid bias, and simultaneous multiplier validity remain open.
